# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We pledge to make participation in this project a harassment-free experience for everyone,
regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics,
gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status,
nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

## Our standards

Behavior that builds this project up:

- Being kind and respectful to other people
- Respecting differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
- Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
- Owning our mistakes, apologizing to those affected, and learning from them
- Focusing on what is best for the project and its users

Behavior that is not acceptable:

- Sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
- Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
- Public or private harassment
- Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their
  explicit permission
- Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

## A note specific to this project

Rampart's subject matter is adversarial by design — `src/adversarial/` exists to attack the
project's own central claim, and a report that breaks it is the most welcome contribution here.
**Attack the code as hard as you like. Never the person who wrote it.** "This classification is
wrong and here is the transaction that proves it" is exactly right. "This is amateur work" is not.

## Enforcement

Report unacceptable behavior to the maintainer via a
[private security advisory](https://github.com/edycutjong/rampart/security/advisories/new) or by
opening an issue if it is not sensitive. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly
and fairly. The maintainer is obligated to respect the privacy and security of anyone who reports
an incident.

Maintainers may remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, issues, and other contributions
that are not aligned with this Code of Conduct, and will communicate the reasons when appropriate.
